items.title: Docker/Systemd alert cooldowns hardcoded (FR-004 drift)
items.problem: engine.go:206 and 248 use a literal 15-minute cooldown for Docker/Systemd transition alerts while FR-004 promises per-rule configurable cooldown. Either add cooldown config to Docker/Systemd rule types or document the divergence in FR-004.

items.title: Stream-encrypt backup files instead of loading whole DB in RAM
items.problem: backup_crypto.go:32 reads entire backup file into memory before AES-GCM. On Pi with low RAM + growing DB, large backups risk OOM. Also encryption runs before max-upload-size check. Replace with chunked AEAD (age, NaCl secretstream, or manual counter+Seal per chunk).

items.title: Prune stale keys from alerts.Engine cooldowns map
items.problem: engine.go:28 cooldowns map grows unbounded for Docker/Systemd keys as container/service names churn. Either prune during evaluate() (drop entries > 2x max cooldown old) or limit the map size.

items.title: ALTER TABLE migrations swallow all errors, not just duplicate-column
items.problem: sqlite.go:183-187 uses _,_ = db.Exec(...) so any failure mode that isn't 'column already exists' is silent. Replace with an error check that logs non-'duplicate column' errors and optionally aborts startup.

items.title: Validate backup local_path server-side (allowlist root, reject symlinks, forbid non-printable chars)
items.problem: server.go:305-308 + sqlite.go:210 accept any path the admin submits. Add validation: (a) must be absolute and under a configured BACKUP_ROOT, (b) reject symlinks, (c) reject NULL bytes and control chars (defense against SQL path injection in VACUUM INTO which cannot be parameterized).

items.title: Log template.Execute error in renderLogin
items.problem: handlers_auth.go:154 ignores tmpl.Execute error. Wrap errors with log.Printf and unify template error handling across handlers.

items.title: Surface missing ULTRON_SECRET_KEY at startup, not lazily
items.problem: internal/database/secrets.go:33-44 — plaintext-storage warning is sync.Once-gated and only fires on first secret use, possibly long after process start. Log the warning unconditionally during cmd/ultron-ap startup, and expose it on /healthz.

items.title: Validate backup LocalPath against an allowed directory
items.problem: internal/database/sqlite.go:205-215 — Backup(dstPath) does not validate the path. SQL escaping is correct, but operator-controlled path can overwrite arbitrary files writable by the daemon. Reject non-absolute paths, .. segments, paths outside a configured backup root; check writability.

items.title: Persist brute-force lockout to SQLite + background cleanup
items.problem: internal/auth/bruteforce.go:29-62 — attempts/locks are in-memory only; restart wipes them. Cleanup is lazy, only on next login attempt. Move to SQLite, run cleanupExpiredBruteForceAttempts on a 5-minute ticker.

items.title: Bind action execution and audit log into one transaction
items.problem: internal/database/actions.go:21-27 — LogAction is a standalone insert. If a Docker action succeeds but the log write fails, audit trail is incomplete. Wrap action + LogAction in one sql.Tx.

items.title: Filter helper log output before returning to web process
items.problem: cmd/ultron-helper/main.go:190-232 — dmesg/ps/journalctl raw output is shipped to the unprivileged web process. ps can include secrets in argv; journal can leak env. Cap byte size, strip sensitive ps fields, define per-source redaction policy.

items.title: Promote CSP from Report-Only to enforced + add report endpoint
items.problem: internal/server/middleware.go:63 — CSP runs Report-Only with no /api/csp-report endpoint. Add the endpoint, log violations one release cycle, then flip the header to enforced.

items.title: Add SO_PEERCRED check in helper IPC (defense-in-depth)
items.problem: cmd/ultron-helper/main.go:43-105 — current Unix socket protection (mode 0o660 + group) is the standard pattern, but adding SO_PEERCRED to verify the connecting process UID matches the configured ultron-ap user provides defense-in-depth against group misconfiguration. Reclassified from BG-004 (audit overcalled severity — current behavior is correct, this is hardening).

items.title: SSE per-IP cap should not blindly trust X-Forwarded-For
items.problem: internal/server/sse.go:479-493 — clientIPFromRequest trusts XFF first value with no proxy allowlist. Real on a proxied deployment but the actual deploy is direct on LAN/VPN, so impact is bounded. Either ignore XFF or only honor when RemoteAddr is in trusted-proxy list. Reclassified from BG-006.

items.title: Log JSON unmarshal errors in notification handlers
items.problem: internal/server/handlers_notifications.go:90 — json.Unmarshal error ignored in handleNotificationTest. If stored config is corrupted, the test sender uses zero-valued cfg fields and the user sees a confusing 'test failed' message instead of 'config corrupted'. Capture err, log it, return a clearer error to the UI. Reclassified from BG-007 (audit overstated impact — no data loss, just UX/observability).

items.title: Feature: lan-devices — discover & track LAN devices via ICMP sweep + ip neigh
items.problem: Pi runs on eth0 in 192.168.1.0/24; gateway/cloudflare/dns probes already cover WAN reachability. Add per-device discovery: 5-min ICMP sweep over /24 + read ip neigh + OUI vendor lookup → device list (IP, MAC, vendor, online/offline, last_seen) persisted in SQLite. No apt installs (uses unprivileged ICMP already enabled via ping_group_range). UI lives at /network. v1 scope: no per-device WiFi signal (router-cooperation required, not feasible from a guest host) and no per-device bandwidth. mDNS hostname enrichment is a v2 follow-up. Cost: ~250 ARP packets in 3s every 5min, negligible Pi/network impact.

items.title: Feature: insights-engine — declarative rules engine producing real-time verdicts across all modules
items.problem: Today Ultron tells you WHAT is happening (CPU 90%, RTT 200ms) but not WHAT IT MEANS. Build a declarative rules engine: each rule = condition over telemetry vars + verdict + severity + recommendation. Reusable across system/network/services/devices. Examples: cpu>=90 AND temp>=75 → 'thermal throttling probable, kill heavy loads'; gateway ok AND cloudflare fail → 'LAN ok, ISP/WAN down'; ram>=90 AND swap>0 → 'memory pressure, inspect processes'. Verdicts surface in dashboard's Operational Indicators section and SSE-stream. Highest-leverage piece: every future module gains diagnostic capability for free by adding rules. Pairs with /help page (BL-018) which becomes the documentation surface for verdict definitions in two voices (technical + non-technical).

items.title: Feature: help-page — glossary & rule-verdict documentation in technical + non-technical voices
items.problem: /help (or /glossary) page documenting Ultron terminology and the verdicts produced by the insights-engine (BL-017). Each entry has two voices: technical (what the metric measures, thresholds, source code path) and non-technical (what it means for the user in plain language). Verdicts from BL-017 deep-link here. Bootstrap content: gateway/cloudflare/dns probe semantics, WAN state machine, jitter/loss/RTT, CPU/RAM/temp thresholds, services/containers health states, VPN peers.

items.title: Task: ui-audit — analysis pass over all Ultron pages, output prioritized punch-list
items.problem: Analysis (NOT build) task. Walk every page (dashboard, network, services, docker, alerts, history, logs, settings, login) and produce a prioritized punch-list of: (1) layout inconsistencies, (2) card-disposition / visual-hierarchy issues, (3) duplicated info, (4) missing pickers / poor input ergonomics (esp. settings), (5) responsive breakpoints. Out of scope: visual redesign. Goal: feed concrete tickets into the settings-revamp feature and any focused UI cleanups. Output: backlog/ui-audit-2026-Q2.md (markdown punch-list, no code).

items.title: Feature: settings-revamp — typed pickers, validation, structure (extends settings-page-ui-improvements)
items.problem: Settings page is the weakest UI in Ultron: raw inputs, no pickers, minimal validation, weak hierarchy. The existing backlog/settings-page-ui-improvements/ folder already has the seed (mobile-first layout, dangerous-action confirmation with countdown, design-token reuse). This BL extends it with: typed input pickers (time, intervals, thresholds, color-coded severity selectors), client+server validation with inline error states, sectioned navigation, search/filter for settings, and exposure of insights-engine (BL-017) rule thresholds as first-class settings once that ships. Sequenced AFTER ui-audit (BL-019) so concrete prioritization comes from the audit punch-list.

items.title: Deploy verification: track binary SHA on Pi
items.problem: No way to verify whether the running prod binary matches the latest committed build. Today: SSH + sha256sum + manual compare. Need a /version endpoint exposing build commit SHA, or a Make target 'deploy-verify' that diffs local arm64 SHA vs remote Pi SHA. Bonus: emit current commit at startup. Also: stale copies exist at /usr/local/bin/ultron-ap and ~/ultron-ap/ — clean up as part of deploy hygiene.

items.title: telegram-message-ux dispatcher wiring (FR-020/021/022/029 partials + NFR-007)
items.problem: Phase 4 of telegram-message-ux declared 5 partials in the implementation_manifest's technical_debt: FR-022 trend hint, FR-020 systemd surface block, FR-021 docker surface block, FR-029 live CPU% in ProcReader, NFR-007 structured 9-field log line. The renderer fully supported these from day 1 — the missing pieces were small dispatcher adapters (read metrics ring buffer + systemd/docker monitors + drive cause derivation + emit obs log line). Without these wired, production messages render the rule context but lack the surface body, trend hint, top-process cause, and structured log audit trail.

items.title: Engine resolve-event emission (FR-018)
items.problem: Phase 1 of telegram-message-ux declared engine-side resolve detection out of scope (no_go_zone item #1). The renderer fully supports resolve templates (✓ RESOLVED + active-for duration, FR-018 AC-018-002). Today the engine only emits fires; when an alert clears naturally (CPU drops below threshold, container goes back to running, service goes back to active), the operator gets nothing — leaving them unsure whether the issue is still ongoing. Wiring resolve detection now: track currently-firing rules in-memory; on each evaluation cycle, for each firing rule, check if condition still holds and emit a resolve event when it doesn't.

items.title: Storm-edit HTTP integration test (FR-024)
items.problem: FR-024 dispatch path is currently covered at the storm.Cache unit level (8 tests) and verified manually in production. The end-to-end TelegramSender.Notify path that decides between sendMessage and editMessageText based on storm.Cache state is exercised in production but not in CI. Add an httptest-based integration test that intercepts api.telegram.org calls, fires the same rule twice within the 60s window, and asserts: sendMessage called exactly once + editMessageText called exactly once + body contains '(2 fires)'.

items.title: Guard insights per-rule state mutation under the service lock
items.problem: internal/insights/insights.go:246-291: cr.state is mutated with s.mu released; safe only single-goroutine. Hold the lock across the eval loop or move per-rule state behind its own mutex.

items.title: Prune processedNet and gate alert-engine shared maps
items.problem: internal/alerts/engine.go:501-502: processedNet grows unbounded (never pruned like cooldowns); prevDocker/prevSystemd/processedNet accessed without consistent locking. Add TTL/prune and gate behind the engine lock.

items.title: Bound SMTP send goroutine lifetime on timeout
items.problem: internal/notify/email.go:87-100: on timeout/ctx-cancel the goroutine keeps running non-ctx-aware smtp.SendMail until the socket times out, leaking goroutine+conn. Use a Dialer with deadline + explicit Close.

items.title: Add per-call timeout to docker refresh requests
items.problem: internal/docker/monitor.go:242,323: refresh passes the process-lifetime ctx to ContainerList/ContainerStats with no per-iteration timeout; a hung docker socket blocks refresh and Stop(). Wrap each call in context.WithTimeout.

items.title: Scope backup retention to backup files, sort by mtime
items.problem: internal/server/server.go:382-397: retention removes files[0:len-retention] assuming lexical==chronological and that every dir entry is a backup; mixed .db/.db.enc or stray files in a custom dir get deleted. Filter to ultron-*.db(.enc) and sort by modtime.

items.title: Reuse long-lived notifier/storm cache in dispatcher
items.problem: internal/notify/dispatcher.go:241,601-621 + storm/storm.go:154: each send rebuilds senders with a fresh storm.Cache and never starts RunJanitor, so storm coalescing never persists across fires and the janitor is dead code. Cache senders across sends; start janitor once.

items.title: Use median/expected cadence for sustained-window coverage
items.problem: internal/insights/lang/lang.go:311-341: cadenceMS uses smallest-ever tick gap (not median); a single fast tick skews when window_ms is satisfied. Track configured/expected cadence or a median.

items.title: Surface brute-force tracker DB failures
items.problem: internal/auth/bruteforce.go:103-105,82-84: IsLocked returns false on lookup error and RecordFailure only logs on write failure; sustained SQLite errors silently disable lockout. Emit a warning/health signal when the tracker is degraded.

items.title: Cover 41 untested ACs from main pipeline (verify-complete gate, blocks reconcile --resolve since rc.173+)
items.problem: aitri verify-complete now hard-gates on AC coverage: 41 acceptance criteria in user_stories have no TC tracing via ac_id (pre-existing debt from the original pipeline; suite itself passes 45/45 TCs). Until covered, the maintenance-path reconcile --resolve cannot advance the baseline.

items.title: AC-015-004: list prior backups in Settings and download the stored encrypted file
items.problem: The only download route (GET /api/settings/backup) generates a FRESH plaintext SQLite snapshot; prior encrypted backups on disk are neither listed nor downloadable. Deferred by the owner on 2026-07-13 ('omite este por ahora') and excluded from the ac-coverage-gaps feature. It is the single remaining untested acceptance criterion — aitri verify-complete will report 1 untested AC until it ships.

items.title: SEC: default deployment ships CSP as Report-Only with script-src 'unsafe-inline' (enforces no XSS protection)
items.problem: middleware.go:96-101 sets Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only unless ULTRON_CSP_ENFORCE=1 (default off); script-src also allows 'unsafe-inline'. Even once enforced the CSP would not stop inline-script XSS. Flip to enforcing after the soak and drop 'unsafe-inline' (nonce/hash the inline scripts in base.html). MEDIUM. Found by aitri audit security 2026-07-14 (RQ-SEC-001).

items.title: SEC: deploy/ultron-ap.sudoers is a parallel root path that bypasses the helper; pironman5 * grants arbitrary root args
items.problem: The sudoers profile grants user ultron NOPASSWD for 'pironman5 *' (trailing wildcard = any args to a root binary the panel never even calls) plus systemctl/shutdown. The Go code never uses sudo — all privilege goes through the validated helper — so if the web process were RCE'd and this file is installed, the attacker sidesteps every cmd/ultron-helper guard. Delete the sudoers file (helper is the sole privilege channel), or replace the pironman5 wildcard with argument-pinned entries. Mitigated: install is a manual step, currently dormant. MEDIUM. RQ-SEC-002.

items.title: SEC: backup encryption key has no length/entropy floor and uses bare unsalted SHA-256 as KDF
items.problem: backup_crypto.go:49-63 backupKeyFromRef does sha256.Sum256(raw) with no salt and no min-length check, while ULTRON_SECRET_KEY (secrets.go:33-46) warns below 16 chars. A weak operator-chosen ULTRON_BACKUP_KEY + a leaked .db.enc (backups upload to Telegram) is offline-brute-forceable. Emit the same <16 warning; ideally a salted KDF (scrypt/argon2, salt in the header). LOW. RQ-SEC-003.

items.title: SEC: /static/ serves a Go autoindex directory listing (unauth), and a .DS_Store is embedded in the binary
items.problem: server.go:572-573 mounts a bare http.FileServer; a dir without index.html gets Go's default autoindex, so GET /static/ and /static/js/ enumerate every file to unauthenticated callers, including a committed .DS_Store (in .gitignore, but go:embed reads the filesystem not git). Wrap the FileServer to 404 on directory paths; delete web/static/.DS_Store before build. LOW. RQ-SEC-004.

items.title: SEC: internal Aitri traceability IDs (FR-/BG-/AC-) ship in client-facing HTML/JS comments
items.problem: base.html:14 (BG-038), settings-backup.html:94 (FR-068), sidebar.js:3 (BG-076), settings.js:2 (FR-065), service-logs.js:1 (FR-081) etc. reach the browser (even /login, unauth). No secrets — only requirement/bug IDs, a minor recon aid. Strip FR-/BG-/AC-/TC- from shipped comments at build time or add a CI grep gate. LOW. RQ-SEC-005.

items.title: SEC: unauthenticated /version discloses build commit and Go toolchain version
items.problem: handlers.go:21 handleVersion (public, server.go:563) returns {version,commit,go:runtime.Version()} with no auth — lets an unauthenticated LAN/Tailscale peer fingerprint the exact build+toolchain for CVE targeting. Move /version behind requireAuth or drop commit/go for anonymous callers; /health stays public+minimal. LOW. RQ-SEC-006.

items.title: UPS: cortes cortos invisibles — sondeo de 10 s y debounce de 30 s
items.problem: Los cortes de red breves no se detectan. Dos causas independientes: (1) el poller pregunta a upsd cada 10 s (ULTRON_UPS_POLL_SECONDS, config.go:16), asi que un corte de <10 s cae entre dos ticks y no genera alerta, ni evento en el historial de cortes, ni punto en la grafica — persist() abre/cierra eventos solo en transiciones vistas al sondear (poller.go persist). (2) Si el UPS absorbe el bajon con su AVR y nunca pasa a OB, ups.status sigue en OL y la unica senal seria input.voltage, cuya alerta exige 30 s continuos fuera de rango (ULTRON_UPS_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS, alerter.go:124) — un bajon de 3 s nunca alerta. El caso 2 es por diseno (AC-021-003, evitar spam en parpadeos), pero el efecto combinado es que el usuario ve cortes reales en casa y Ultron no los reporta ni los registra. Reportado por el owner 2026-09-04. La alerta de corte en si NO tiene debounce: cuando el corte dura mas de un tick, la latencia es ~10 s + ~2 s del driver NUT, lo cual esta bien.
items.behavior: Un corte de red de cualquier duracion que el UPS reconozca debe quedar registrado en el historial de cortes y en la grafica, y disparar notificacion segun las reglas de storm/dedup existentes.
items.decisions: Opcion A (parche de config, sin pipeline): bajar ULTRON_UPS_POLL_SECONDS a 2-3 en /etc/ultron-ap/ultron-ap.env. Detecta cortes de >=3 s pero multiplica las muestras: a 2 s son ~1.3M filas/mes vs ~260k hoy, con retencion de 30 dias. No cubre el caso 2. Opcion B (correcta, cambio funcional -> aitri feature init): NUT ya conoce el evento al instante; que upsmon/upssched empuje ONBATT/ONLINE a Ultron en vez de que Ultron sondee. Requiere endpoint de ingesta autenticado y config de NUT en el Pi. Pendiente decision del owner.
items.acceptance: Un corte simulado de 3 s aparece en el historial de cortes y dispara la notificacion correspondiente; el sondeo periodico sigue siendo el fallback si el canal de eventos falla.

items.title: E2E de navegador: decidir harness o aceptar los ACs como deuda permanente
items.problem: 79 TCs declarados como type=e2e en todo el proyecto y cero runner de navegador — no hay package.json, ni Playwright, ni chromedp. La mayoria no lo necesita: NUT_UPS (11 e2e), insights-engine (2) y network-tile (2) los resolvieron como tests HTTP en Go con httptest y pasan. Los que si lo necesitan son 7 ACs de help-page (AC-050-002/003, AC-051-002/003, AC-054-002/003, AC-056-002) y ~13 de settings-revamp, porque piden geometria real (boxPlain.y < boxTech.y, solape horizontal >=80%), javaScriptEnabled=false, y la trayectoria del alfa de una animacion :target a los 1500ms. Eso exige un motor de layout, no se simula con httptest. Consecuencia hoy: ambos features estan en 5/5 verde, pero si se re-camina su pipeline por cualquier motivo quedan atascados en 4/5 contra esos ACs. Por eso sus 2 upgrade findings (runner con 'go test -C ../..') se dejaron sin arreglar el 2026-09-04. ACTUALIZACION 2026-09-06: el escenario previsto ocurrio. Se arreglaron los 2 upgrade findings (test_runner pasado a rutas relativas al feature dir, la forma que ya usa network-tile), eso produjo drift en 04_BUILD_REPORT.json, el owner re-aprobo build en TTY y el verify se reabrio. Al re-correr el gate fresco, help-page quedo en 4/5 con 7 ACs y settings-revamp en 4/5 con 13 ACs (20 en total, coincide con lo estimado). La raiz sigue verde 86/86 y Deployable. Los 2 upgrade findings ya NO existen: ese coste esta pagado y es irreversible, asi que la Opcion A ya no devuelve ambos features a 5/5 por si sola — hace falta declarar technical_debt en sus build reports o poner el harness. Decidido con el owner el 2026-09-06: seguir con las notas de docker-via-helper y net-sample-retention primero; esto se cierra en un ciclo aparte.
items.behavior: Cada AC declarado tiene un test que lo ejecuta de verdad, o una decision explicita y fechada de que no se verifica y por que.
items.decisions: Opcion A (aceptar deuda, coste cero): registrar en el 04_BUILD_REPORT.json de help-page y settings-revamp una entrada technical_debt que declare esos ACs como no verificables sin harness, siguiendo el precedente que insights-engine ya tiene documentado para TC-IE-006h/006f/006e. Los 2 upgrade findings se quedan; son falsos positivos verificados del checker, que no modela el flag -C de go test. Opcion B (chromedp): se queda en Go, sin stack JS, sin package.json; anade una dependencia de chromium en CI. Es la mas coherente con este repo. Opcion C (Playwright): mejor API para asertar geometria y alfa computado, pero mete Node y node_modules en un proyecto que hoy no tiene ninguno. Nota: SSH al Pi no es una via — los tests levantan el servidor en proceso, asi que la app bajo prueba es local; apuntar los e2e al binario desplegado probaria el commit equivocado y CI no lo alcanzaria. Por CLAUDE.md, B y C son cambio funcional y van por aitri feature init.
items.acceptance: O bien existe un runner e2e que cubre los ~20 ACs de help-page y settings-revamp y ambos features vuelven a 5/5 tras re-caminar el pipeline; o bien esos ACs estan marcados como deuda aceptada en sus build reports y esta decision queda cerrada por escrito.

items.title: FR-008 raiz: retirar la mitad Docker de Service controls tras docker-via-helper
items.problem: La feature docker-via-helper retira los controles start/stop/restart de contenedores Docker de la web app, porque la frontera de seguridad acordada tras el hallazgo C2 de la auditoria 2026-09-05 es que la web app no pueda actuar sobre Docker (el helper expone Docker en SOLO lectura). Eso vuelve falso el criterio AC-008-002 del FR-008 raiz ('Start, Stop, Restart buttons per Docker container') y deja huerfano el TC-008e declarado ('Docker stop logs the action with timestamp'), que ademas nunca tuvo implementacion en Go. Ningun test verde se rompe: TC-008a prueba /services (systemd), no contenedores, y no existe ningun test que referencie los handlers de control de Docker. La raiz sigue 86/86 y Deployable. El desajuste es de especificacion, no de codigo: el PRD raiz promete botones que ya no existen.
items.behavior: FR-008 cubre solo los controles de servicios systemd. Los controles de contenedores Docker no aparecen como requisito, y TC-008e no existe o queda declarado como retirado con su motivo.
items.decisions: Decidido con el owner el 2026-09-06: NO enmendar ahora. 'aitri run-phase requirements --feedback' en la raiz cascadea e invalida arquitectura, tests, build y deploy, que hoy estan 5/5 y Deployable, y el precedente de help-page/settings-revamp ese mismo dia mostro que reabrir una fase destapa gates latentes. Se prioriza desplegar las dos notas de la Pi. Cuando se abra: quitar AC-008-002 y el TC-008e del alcance de FR-008, reescribir su descripcion para que hable solo de servicios systemd, y verificar que la cascada no deja ACs sin cobertura.
items.acceptance: FR-008 no menciona control de contenedores Docker, TC-008e no figura como test pendiente, y la raiz vuelve a quedar 5/5 con verify verde tras la cascada.
